title: Affine Zariski comparison with the standard ring naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $f:U\to V$ be its induced morphism of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme]. Put $P_0=R[x_b\mid b\in B]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $\alpha_0:P_0\twoheadrightarrow B$ send $x_b$ to $b$, and set $J=\ker\alpha_0$. Define the standard ring naive cotangent complex
$$C_{B/R}=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{[h]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dh}B\otimes_{P_0}\Omega_{P_0/R}]$$
in degrees $-1,0$, zero elsewhere, using [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On the Zariski site of $U$, let $\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}=\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal O_U/f^{-1}\mathcal O_V}$ be the sheaf naive complex $K_{\mathcal O_U}$ of [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison], with inverse image [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. For a $B$-module use its associated Zariski module sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], functorially as in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], and apply this functor termwise to $C_{B/R}$. There is a canonical map of complexes
$$\widetilde{C_{B/R}}\longrightarrow\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}$$
which is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No finiteness, Noetherian or flatness hypothesis on $R\to B$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D0I, lemma-NL-affine, specialized to X = Spec B and Y = Spec R; definition-netherlander and algebra.tex section-netherlander for the explicitly written standard presentation.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_U$ and $K=\mathrm{NL}^{\mathrm{Zar}}_{U/V}$. The inverse-image adjunction unit gives $R\to\mathcal A(U)$. Restricting coefficients and sending $x_b$ to the variable indexed by the global section $b\in\mathcal B(U)=B$ gives $R[B]\to\mathcal A[\mathcal B](U)$, compatible with evaluation to $B$. Thus $J$ maps into the kernel sheaf; products in $J^2$ map into its square. It gives $J/J^2\to K^{-1}(U)$ and, by universal differentials, $B\otimes_{R[B]}\Omega_{R[B]/R}\to K^0(U)$, sending $b\otimes\mathrm dh$ to $b\,\mathrm d(h')$. Since both differentials send $[h]$ to $\mathrm dh$, this is a chain map. Apply the tilde/global-sections adjunction termwise. Naturality of its Hom bijection carries the chain identity to a chain identity, giving the claimed canonical map $\eta:\widetilde{C_{B/R}}\to K$.

source.place: Tag 0D0I (lemma-NL-affine), construction from sections and Schemes Tag 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions); modules.tex section-netherlander

proof.text: Fix a point $p\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ and put $q=\varphi^{-1}(p)$ for $\varphi:R\to B$. The affine stalk-localization statement identifies $\mathcal B_p=B_p$ and $(\mathcal O_V)_q=R_q$ through the germ maps. The inverse-image stalk statement identifies $\mathcal A_p$ with $R_q$ and carries the germ of the adjunction-unit image of $r\in R$ to $r/1$. The tilde-stalk localization statement identifies $(\widetilde{C_{B/R}})_p$ with the termwise localization $(C_{B/R})_p$, carrying a global element $c$ to $c/1$. Functoriality makes this an identification of complexes. The map $R\to B_p$ extends to $R_q\to B_p$: if $r\notin q$ then $\varphi(r)\notin p$, so it is a unit in $B_p$. No assertion about $\mathcal A(U)$ being a localization is needed.

The polynomial differential basis identifies the displayed tensor-differential models with the standard free-module models used by the following two homology nodes, and its formula for $\mathrm dh$ identifies the differentials. Consider the canonical chain map $a:(C_{B/R})_p\to C_{B_p/R}$ induced by $b\mapsto b/1$. Exactness of module localization identifies its degree $-1$ cohomology with the map $(H_1(L_{B/R}))_p\to H_1(L_{B_p/R})$, which is an isomorphism by the existing $H_1$-localization node, with multiplicative subset $B\setminus p$. In degree $0$, the cokernel/differentials node identifies the source and target cohomology with $(\Omega_{B/R})_p$ and $\Omega_{B_p/R}$; the induced map sends $\mathrm db/s$ to $s^{-1}\mathrm d(b/1)$, so differential localization makes it an isomorphism. All other cohomology groups vanish because both complexes have only degrees $-1,0$. Thus $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This obtains the full quasi-isomorphism from the two existing cohomology clauses of Tag 00S7 rather than creating another localization node.

source.place: Tag 0D0I (lemma-NL-affine), target-localization part of the stalk argument, algebra.tex Tag 00S7 (lemma-localize-NL)

proof.text: Apply base localization to $A=R$, $S=R\setminus q$ and the map $R_q\to B_p$ just constructed. It gives the canonical quasi-isomorphism $b:C_{B_p/R}\to C_{B_p/R_q}$. Apply the sheaf-naive stalk comparison to $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ at $p$: it identifies $K_p$ with $C_{B_p/R_q}$ in $D(B_p)$. Under this comparison and the tilde-stalk identification, $\eta_p$ is $ba$. Indeed a polynomial $h\in R[B]$ goes to the polynomial obtained by $r\mapsto r/1$ and $x_c\mapsto x_{c/1}$; its conormal class goes to the class of that polynomial and $c\otimes\mathrm dh$ goes to $(c/1)\otimes\mathrm d(h')$. These are exactly the sectionwise germ formulas in the stalk-comparison statement. The equalities hold first for global generators and then for fractions $z/s$ by $B_p$-linearity. Therefore $\eta_p$ induces isomorphisms on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0D0I (lemma-NL-affine), base-localization and stalk-comparison parts: algebra.tex Tag 07BS and modules.tex Tag 0D09

proof.text: Stalk exactness commutes with the kernels, images and cokernels defining cohomology, so $H^i(\eta)_p=H^i(\eta_p)$ for every $i$ and $p$. These maps are isomorphisms by the preceding steps. The kernels and cokernels of $H^i(\eta)$ therefore have zero stalks; the exactness-detection clause applied to $0\to\ker H^i(\eta)\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{coker}H^i(\eta)\to0$ makes them zero sheaves. Hence $H^i(\eta)$ is an isomorphism, so $\eta$ is a quasi-isomorphism and becomes an isomorphism in the derived category. If $B$ is the zero ring, $U$ is empty and the same stalk-detection argument applies vacuously. None of the inputs required finite presentation, Noetherianity or flatness of $B$ over $R$.
